content:
I searched Loogle for (?a)⁻¹ = ?b → ?a = (?b)⁻¹.

The response is

(deterministic) timeout at `whnf`, maximum number of heartbeats (200000) has been reached

Note: Use `set_option maxHeartbeats <num>` to set the limit.(invalid MessageData.lazy, missing context)

(I also tried this without the parentheses in the query; I added those in because when I got the timeout, I assumed there was some kind of grammar error involved.)

Am I missing something? How do I run this search without crashing Loogle?
Can you #xy it ? Might be helpful to know the intent of the search as well !

The problem I'm asking about is that I'm getting Loogle timeouts on what I thought were simple, correctly-formed queries. Just now I got one on ?x ∈ ?a → ?x ∈ ?b → ?a = ?b. Same response:

(deterministic) timeout at `isDefEq`, maximum number of heartbeats (200000) has been reached

Note: Use `set_option maxHeartbeats <num>` to set the limit.(invalid MessageData.lazy, missing context)

These are simple enough results that I can provide them myself. I'm not concerned about finding the answers. But I need to know how to correctly phrase a Loogle query! Sometimes I search for results I don't want to derive on the spot.
Either there's a bug in the server, or I've forgotten the query syntax. Is there a bug in the server? If not, what went wrong in my queries?

How to phrase the search correctly , also depends on what you are looking for ( especially in the case of time outs ). How about @loogle (?A : Type _) → ( _ : Subsingleton ?A) → (?x : ?A ∈ (?a : Set ?A)) → ?x ∈ ?b → ?a = ?b

:exclamation:

type expected, got
  (?x : ?A ∈ ?a)

Oops , on phone

Timeout doesn’t mean your query is wrong , just not specific enough.

A simp for example may be entirely legal in its syntax , but it can also loop and reach the same kind of error if done wrong.

@loogle (?A : Type _) → ( _ : Subsingleton ?A) → ((?x : ?A) ∈ (?a : Set ?A)) → ?x ∈ ?b → ?a = ?b

I checked this one and it works ( though finds nothing )

Essentially without more info, you start with two meta variables of unknown types , which you must then unify the membership notation for which basically is unifying a compatible function with whatever types it works with ( since you haven’t specified ).

So ultimately it goes on a wild goose chase with too many intertwining possibilities, you can try run it locally and increase heartbeats (though that may be futile in this case) .

There was a thread about this, but otherwise it goes to the Loogle server which simply won’t allow huge unoptimised queries like that.

Notably I believe basically every single type A has one such notation defined, for Set A.

So you can iterate this forever and blow up your search, Set A ∈ Set (Set A) , Set (Set A) ∈ Set (Set (Set A)) ?

whnf stands for weak head normal form and is a way for metaprograms to avoid unfolding too much .
That's why you don’t even need to try that hard , ?a ∈ ?A does the same (as does ?a = (?b)⁻¹ )
I get a similar timeout trying to search for (?a = ?b) = (?b = ?a). I don't understand what the right way to phrase this query is.
In this case it works when using an equivalence instead: (_ = _) ↔ (_ = _)
